adjacency-precedence|PROOF: cells constrained by how many neighbours carry a value, or by what the cells to the left and above them carry
algfield|PROOF: a general algebraic function field: nested radicals, implicit or reversion g.f.s
all-values-subblock|PROOF: subblocks with a prescribed number of distinct values, counted up to renaming and using every letter
array-permutation|PROOF: permutations of the CELLS of a fixed-width array in which every cell moves by one of a short list of offsets -- a permanent, carried as which images inside a bounded window are already taken
bounded-difference-triangle|PROOF: a fixed triangle over 0..n whose condition constrains differences only: translation splits the arrays into finitely many classes, a class of spread s holds max(0, n+1-s) of them, and the spread is bounded by the graph diameter, so the count is exactly linear from a point known in advance
budget|PROOF: a cell condition with an exception budget, counted up to relabelling
canonical-subblock|PROOF: the entry asks two things at once: a condition on every subblock, which a window of consecutive rows decides, and that new values be introduced in row major order, which is not local at all -- it counts colourings up to renaming. The whole prefix enters only through how many values have been introduced so far, so one extra integer in the state carries it exactly, and the count is again a walk count
capped-pair-count|PROOF: a global count of adjacent pairs summing to a value, carried in the state by capping it
cell-condition-pattern|PROOF: a cell condition stated through equality alone, counted up to renaming the letters
cell-condition|PROOF: a condition on each cell and its neighbours, decided in a three-row window
chessboard-colour-class|PROOF: white- and black-square subarrays: a diagonal step never changes the colour of a cell, so the two colour classes are independent and the count is a walk over the cells of one of them
circular-coloring|PROOF: proper colourings of a grid circular in one direction, counted up to renaming the colours
clashing-pair|PROOF: neighbouring cells forbidden to carry values summing to m, with the renaming clauses that pick one array per class carried in state
clockwise-perimeter|PROOF: conditions read round the clockwise perimeter of every 2 X 2 subblock: the pattern its corners spell, the number of edge increases each way round, and how those counts compare with the neighbouring subblocks'
closedform-direct|PROOF: a posted closed form compared against the posted generating function
closedform-name|PROOF: the known side is the entry's NAME rather than a formula line
closedform|PROOF: a posted closed form decided by the theory of hypergeometric terms
column-domination|PROOF: the entry forbids any column from sitting above the one before it in EVERY row, which no bounded window decides; but it is a conjunction of independent per-row facts, so one bit per adjacent column pair carries it and the state is that bit mask alone, however large the alphabet
common-sum|PROOF: an unnamed common subblock sum removed by splitting the count over its possible values
commuting-subblock|PROOF: neighbouring K X K subblocks commuting as matrices, or none of them commuting
consecutive-triple|PROOF: consecutive triples along rows, columns and diagonals holding a prescribed number of distinct values, counted up to renaming
defective|PROOF: defective colourings: a budget of monochromatic pairs carried in the state, counted up to relabelling
diagonal|PROOF: the generating function derived from a coefficient-extraction definition
digit-divisibility|PROOF: rows and columns read as base-b numbers and required to be divisible, or not, by given moduli
disproof|DISPROOF: a conjecture shown FALSE, with the recurrence that holds instead
distance-inequality|PROOF: no two cells within a stated distance may agree, counted up to renaming
distance-repeat|PROOF: the entry asks that every value be repeated, or never be repeated, at exactly its own city-block distance; the reach is bounded by the alphabet, so a window of that many lines carries the question, one bit per cell recording whether its partner has been found yet
edge-count-pattern|PROOF: equal-edge conditions on the subblocks, counted up to renaming the letters
edge-count|PROOF: the number of clockwise, counterclockwise or rightwards-and-downwards edge increases in every 2 X 2 subblock
equate|PROOF: a conjectured closed form or g.f., proved against a recurrence derived from the entry
forbidden-run|PROOF: runs of equal or of strictly increasing entries forbidden along the directions of a grid
funceq-mod|PROOF: a defining functional equation reduced mod k, then closed by uniqueness of its recursion
gauss-congruence|PROOF: the same reduction, plus x^(p^r) = x^(p^(r-1)) mod p^r, for every shift
gf-conjecture|PROOF: the entry's only conjecture is a generating function: the count is a walk count so its generating function is rational of bounded degree, and comparing enough coefficients of two such functions proves they are equal
gf-implies-rec|PROOF: the recurrence follows from a generating function the entry records as fact
global-count|PROOF: a global count of marked adjacent pairs carried in the state, then a walk count
graph-adjacency-array|PROOF: arrays whose cells carry vertices of a fixed graph -- the faces or vertices of a cube or icosahedron, a triangular patch of the lattice, or a listed edge set -- with adjacent cells joined by an edge
graph-array-lumped|PROOF: the same graph-coloured arrays with too many slices to carry one by one, run instead on the orbits of slices under the automorphism group of the graph
holonomic|PROOF: a posted closed form against a derived holonomic recurrence
image-count|PROOF: the number of distinct indicator arrays a cell condition produces: an image count, made a walk count by determinisation
index-change|PROOF: grid permutations with a bounded index change, as a matching turned into a walk
king-move|PROOF: a condition on every cell's king-move neighbourhood, boundaries included
lattice-count|PROOF: a nondecreasing row of plus and minus ones is fixed by one number, so the entry condition collapses to a linear equation on a box of lattice points and the arrays vanish; the count is then a quasi-polynomial whose degree and period are both named, which bounds the order of a recurrence it must satisfy
lex-subblock-statistic|PROOF: each 2 X 2 subblock reduced to one number -- a determinant, a permanent, a sum, or an order statistic -- with the rows and columns of the derived array in lexicographic order
local-array-condition|PROOF: the entry imposes a condition that a bounded amount of state carries down the array -- a window of three consecutive lines for the local ones, or a row sum together with one flag per adjacent column pair for the two that compare whole rows and whole columns
logexp|PROOF: a transcendental e.g.f., in a differential module over Q(x)
matrix-subblock|PROOF: the determinant, permanent or trace of every 2 X 2 subblock: singular, all equal, differing from a neighbour, or monotone
minmax-median|PROOF: the smallest and largest of the four entries of a 2 X 2 block, summed, against the sum of the other two
modular-neighbour|PROOF: every cell required to see neighbours carrying the next and the previous value modulo m
monotone-statistic|PROOF: a statistic of short runs of cells, whose derived array is required to be monotone in a named direction
monotone-subblock|PROOF: a statistic of every 2 X 2 or 3 X 3 subblock monotone along named directions of the subblock grid
neighbour-arithmetic|PROOF: what a cell asks of the cells around it: not their average, not matched by a strict majority of them, not beaten by one, not equal to both the cell above and the cell left, or equal to the sum of one of two groups of them
neighbour-condition|PROOF: the entry constrains each element by the elements one step away from it, so three consecutive lines decide the condition on the middle one; the pairs of consecutive lines are the vertices of a finite digraph and the arrays are its walks, with the array boundary honest -- a missing neighbour is not a neighbour
neighbour-existential|PROOF: what a cell demands that SOME neighbour of it look like: one at least as large, one of a named value, an allowed number of them, or its own value plus and minus one
neighbour-set|PROOF: a condition on every cell over the neighbour set the entry names
occupancy-image|PROOF: occupancy patterns reachable when every unit moves to a neighbouring cell or stays put: counted by determinising the map from movement to occupancy
occupancy-turn|PROOF: occupancy arrays of a grid of tokens each moving one step, with the turn a token makes on arrival constrained
offset-inequality|PROOF: no cell equal to the cells at a fixed list of offsets, counted up to renaming
order-cond|PROOF: monotone and unimodal conditions along rows, columns and diagonals, with the fallen bits carried in the state
order-flag|PROOF: a neighbour condition plus a first-occurrence ordering clause carried as a flag in the state
order-recovery|PROOF: the conjecture's own text was unavailable; the recurrence was recovered and shown unique
order-statistic|PROOF: a signed sum of the order statistics of every 2 X 2 subblock taking one common value
ore-complete|PROOF: complete annihilation, tested in the Ore algebra Q(n)[N]
ore|PROOF: division of one posted operator by another
pair-sum-order|PROOF: two derived arrays of pair sums, ordered monotonically, lexicographically, or by a nonvanishing determinant
parity-difference|PROOF: a parity that reaches back to the top of the array but is carried by one bit per column, or a condition on differences between a cell and the cells one step away, which three consecutive lines decide
parity|PROOF: a posted closed form split on the parity of n, then decided by hypergeometric terms
pattern-avoidance|PROOF: short absolute or relative patterns forbidden along the rows, columns and diagonals of a grid
pattern-neighbour|PROOF: a cell condition counted up to relabelling, by falling-factorial inversion
pattern-subblock|PROOF: a 3 X 3 subblock condition counted up to relabelling, by falling-factorial inversion
perimeter-cycle|PROOF: the clockwise perimeter cycle of every 2 X 3 and 3 X 2 subblock: how many of its six steps go up
planepartition-box|PROOF: matrices over 0..n with rows and columns nondecreasing: reversed, they are the plane partitions in a box, so MacMahon's product applies and telescopes to a polynomial; the entry's own expression then follows by an identity between polynomials of bounded degree
quadratic|DISPROOF: a separate argument for that one problem
quadratic|PROOF: the residual test over one square root, or none
ray-sum|PROOF: no entry equal, modulo m, to a constant plus the sum of the entries along a ray out of it
reciprocal-link|PROOF: cells linked reciprocally to themselves or to a fixed number of neighbours: degree-constrained subgraphs of a grid
relabelling|PROOF: arrays counted up to relabelling: patterns recovered by falling-factorial inversion, then a lumped walk count
repeated-value|PROOF: the repeated values of each row and column, in the order they occur, required to stand in a prescribed relation
rowmajor-across-columns|PROOF: a clause on the order of first occurrences in ROW major order, on an array the walk has to cross column by column: the state carries each named value's least row and the order those least rows were reached, and the clause is tested only at the end
section|PROOF: an entry equated to an m-section of another entry, decided from both entries' facts
self-count|PROOF: every entry equal to the number of its own neighbours standing in a stated relation to it
stirling-phi|PROOF: e.g.f. G(e^x-1) with G integral: a(n) mod k is an integer combination of n -> i^n
subblock-3x3|PROOF: a 3 X 3 subblock condition, whose state is a pair of consecutive lines
subblock-coloring|PROOF: the 2 X 2 subblocks properly coloured by a statistic of their entries: neighbours must differ
subblock-condition|PROOF: the entry constrains every subblock of a fixed size, or every pair of neighbouring subblocks, so a bounded window of consecutive lines decides it; the admissible windows are the vertices of a finite digraph and the arrays are its walks
subblock-content|PROOF: a property of the nine entries of a 3 X 3 subblock -- their sum, the multiset of how often each value occurs, the determinant, the pairwise absolute differences, or that every block agrees with every other
subblock-difference|PROOF: a statistic of every 2 X 2 subblock differing from its neighbours by exactly a fixed amount
subblock-line-sum|PROOF: the sums along the rows, columns and diagonals of every K X K window of a grid, constrained or compared
subblock-matrix|PROOF: every K X K subblock of a matrix idempotent, or of equal population or permanent
subblock-neighbour|PROOF: a subblock statistic compared with its neighbours': none equal, some equal, exactly one or two equal, or bounded difference
subblock-statistic-neighbour|PROOF: a number read off the two diagonals of a small subblock -- a difference or a sum of corner entries, or of diagonal extremes -- required to differ from the same number at the overlapping subblock one step over
symmetric-sum-zero|PROOF: square symmetric matrices whose 2 X 2 subblocks all sum to zero: solving that linear condition makes the matrix a function of its own diagonal, and the count collapses to a walk on sequences
table-column|PROOF: a table's column recurrences, each column being a fixed-width array count
table-order-recovery|PROOF: a table line whose recurrence was unwritten, recovered from its stated order and shown unique
telescoping-boundary|PROOF: creative telescoping with the boundary and range corrections carried through
telescoping|PROOF: a recurrence derived from the summand by creative telescoping
transfer-matrix|PROOF: an array count rebuilt as walks in a digraph, then the recurrence annihilated exactly
triangle-quasipolynomial|PROOF: a triangle of FIXED shape over the alphabet 0..n: the alphabet grows, not the shape, so there is no digraph to walk; inclusion-exclusion over the adjacent pairs gives an exact quasi-polynomial of period 2 and the recurrence follows by polynomial division
value-neighbour|PROOF: every cell carrying one stated value required to have a neighbour carrying another
walk-closed-form|PROOF: an explicit closed form, turned into the recurrence it satisfies
white-squares|PROOF: only the cells with i+j even carry a value and their diagonal neighbours are again such cells, so the white squares form a board of their own; each must have a neighbour holding a prescribed function of its value, which three consecutive lines settle
